texts.preamble: Vardhman Jain vs Richi Singhal on 17 March, 2025 In The Court Of Ms. Sheetal Chaudhary Pradhan Additional Sessions Judge-02, South-East District Saket Courts, New Delhi Criminal Appeal No. 258/2024 Ps- Amar Colony U/Sec. 29 Pwdv Act In the matter of :- 1. Vardhman Jain S/o Late Sh. Padam Jain 2 . Smt. Suman Lata W/o Late Sh. Padam Jain Both Residents Of : H. No. 659, Sector 15 Faridabad, Haryana- 121007. .... Appellants Versus Mrs. Richi Singhal W/o Sh. Vardhaman Jain D/o Smt. Kanta Singhal H. No. 659, First Floor, Sector 15, Faridabad, Haryana- 121007. .... Respondent Date of Institution : 05.08.2024 Date of Final Arguments : 28.02.2025 Date of Decision : 17.03.2025 Decision : [LEAKAGE_MASK].
texts.facts: "The complainant (Richi Singhal) and respondent no. 1 (Vardhman Jain) got married as per Hindu rites and ceremonies on 20.05.2009 at Jhankar Banquet, Asiad CA No. 258/2024 Vardhman Jain & Anr. Vs. Richi Singhal Page no. 2 of 21 Tower, Khelgaon, New Delhi. Respondent No. 2 & Respondent No. 3 are the father-in-law and mother- in-law of the complainant respectively. After getting married to respondent no. 1, complainant stayed at her matrimonial home at Faridabad with respondents till 03.04.2015 where the petitioner was tortured and harassed on day-to-day basis by all the three respondents from day one of her marriage. A baby girl namely Samriddhi Jain was born on 27.10.2010 from the said wedlock. The complainant was tortured from day one of her marriage to extort dowry from her mother. After the birth of a daughter, the harassment of the complainant at the hands of the respondents, increased manyfold. Right after baby girl was born, all the three respondents started cursing and harassing her every day on one pretext or the other. All three respondents started beating and torturing the complainant for the reason that she could not give birth to a boy. The complainant always protested against the violent & cruel acts of respondents who threatened to leave the complainant and her baby girl alone and to remarry a woman who can give birth to a boy. The respondents forced the complainant to consult different doctors without having any health problems in order to succeed in their nefarious design of collecting various opinions CA No. 258/2024 Vardhman Jain & Anr. Vs. Richi Singhal Page no. 3 of 21 of different psychiatrists to create wrongful proofs of mental illness of the complainant from time to time. Even prescriptions, documents and the signatures of the complainant were forged to create wrongful proofs of mental illness of the complainant. Further, the complainant was forced to do the entire household task alone from morning till late at night without any type of help from any domestic servant. On many occasions, the complainant was given various drugs in food and drinks to disturb her mental status just to prove that the complainant is suffering from mental problems to blackmail her mother to extort money and even get rid of the complainant as she had given birth to a girl child. Even ambulance from various hospitals were called upon to forcefully send the complainant to mental hospitals on many occasions without any cause just to get rid of the complainant. The complainant along with her daughter suffered immense humiliation at the hands of all the three respondents. After being continuously harassed, abused and beaten for more than six years, the complainant decided to take legal help. Hence, the present complaint case was filed". Thereafter, on 23.10.2019, respondent no. 1 undertook to pay an interim maintenance of Rs. 10,000/- per month to the complainant and their minor child towards their welfare from the month of January 2017 till further orders. The said order dated 23.10.2019 was challenged by the respondent no. 1 which was upheld by the order of Ld. Sessions Courts vide its order dated 28.01.2020. 6. As per order dated 29.05.2024, the respondent no. 2 namely Padam Jain has expired and thus he was dropped from array of the parties. 7. Record reveals that complainant led her evidence and examined herself as CW1 and tendered her evidence by way of affidavit Ex.CW1/A and also relied upon the documents Ex.CW1/1 to Ex.CW1/19 and Mark A and Mark B. Despite giving opportunities, CW1 was not cross-examined and therefore vide order dated 03.01.2023, right to cross-examine the complainant was closed and vide order dated 03.01.2023, complainant's evidence was closed. 8. Respondents did not not lead any evidence and therefore, vide order dated 20.10.2023, respondent's evidence was closed and matter was fixed for final arguments. 9. After hearing final arguments, matter was reserved for pronouncement of judgment and impugned order was passed on 04.07.2024. CA No. 258/2024 Vardhman Jain & Anr. Vs. Richi Singhal Page no. 5 of 21 10. Aggrieved to the aforesaid impugned judgment dated 04.07.2024 passed by Ld. Trial Court, respondent no. 1/ husband has challenged the said order by way of present appeal. Respondent has taken following grounds to challenge impugned order passed by Ld. Trial Court :- a) That impugned judgment dated 04.07.2024 passed by Ld. Trial Court is bad in law, without application of any judicial mind and is based on presumptions, conjectures and surmises and contrary to documents on record, settled law. b) That Ld. Trial Court did not appreciate that respondent and the baby girl are residing with the appellant no. 1 in the first floor of house no. 659, Sector-15, Faridabad, Haryana since marriage and only for certain time resided at rented accommodation. c) That Ld. Trial Court did not appreciate that minor baby girl Samridhi Jain who is now about 14 years is in class IX and all her expenses like school fees, tuition fees, uniforms, books, stationary and other curricular activities, clothes and medicines are born by the appellants since birth and she is getting education in DPS Faridabad. Moreover it is the appellant who "pick and drop" his minor daughter to the school regularly. Vardhman Jain vs Richi Singhal on 17 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151189958/ 3 d) That Ld. Trial Court did not appreciate that appellants are paying groceries, fruits, milk, vegetables, medicines etc. including electricity and water bills of the first floor where respondent is residing with the appellant and minor girl. CA No. 258/2024 Vardhman Jain & Anr. Vs. Richi Singhal Page no. 6 of 21 e) That Ld. Trial Court did not appreciate that appellant and the respondent filed their Income Affidavit in August, 2018 and December, 2018 respectively along with all necessary relevant documents. g) That as per records, the respondent no. 1/ husband is not earning more than Rs. 25,000/- pm and working as Manager in Vardhman International Public School, Faridabad which runs under "Swami Vivekanand Educational Society". Further respondent no. 3 (mother-in-law of complainant) bears the expenditure of respondent no. 1/ husband, complainant and the minor daughter. h) That as per records, the complainant has stated in her complaint under DV Act regarding living at Lajpat Nagar where as the fact remains that she has been residing with the respondents/ husband at his expenses at the matrimonial home and complainant had not disclosed the true fact before Ld. Trial Court. CA No. 258/2024 Vardhman Jain & Anr. Vs. Richi Singhal Page no. 7 of 21 i) That Ld. Trial Court did not appreciate that complainant was residing along with respondent no. 1/ husband at her matrimonial home at Faridabad right through the inception of the marriage till now even at the time of filing of the complaint. 11. In addition to the above grounds, it has been argued that impugned order is vitiated by fatal infirmities and it prayed that impugned judgment dated 04.07.2024 in CC no. 634593/2016 must be [LEAKAGE_MASK].
texts.arguments: Counsel for the complainant has argued that impugned order passed by Ld. Trial Court, is legally correct and needs no interference and has been passed after considering the records of this case. Where a woman is subjected to cruelty by her husband or her relatives for demand of dowry, it is an offence u/sec. 498A of the Indian Penal Code. CA No. 258/2024 Vardhman Jain & Anr. Vs. Richi Singhal Page no. 9 of 21 15. The Act inter-alia provides for more effective protection or the right of woman guaranteed under the constitution who are victims of the domestic violence of any kind occurring within the shared household. According to the Act, any harm, injury to health, safety, life, limb or well being or any other act or threatening or coercion etc. by any adult member of the family, constitutes domestic violence. Further, the act also contemplates that any woman who is or has been in a domestic relationship, if she is subjected to any domestic violence can file a complaint u/sec. 12 of the PWDV Act. This Act also covers those woman who are or have been in relationship with the abuser where both parties have live together in a shared household and a relative by consanguinity, marriage or through a relationship in the nature of marriage or adoption. 18. For computing the maintenance, the following test have been laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in Jasbir Kaur Sehgal vs. District Judge, Dehradun & Ors. 1997 (7) SCC 7, wherein it has been observed that: "No set formula can be laid for fixing the amount of maintenance. It has, in the very nature of things, to depend on the facts and circumstances of each case. Some scope for leverage can, however, be always there. The court has to consider the status of the parties, their respective needs, the capacity of the husband to pay having regard to his reasonable expenses for his own maintenance and of those he is obliged under the law and statutory but involuntary payments or deductions. The amount of maintenance fixed for the wife or children should be such as she can live in reasonable comfort considering her status and the mode of life she was used to when she lived with her husband and also that she does not feel handicapped in the prosecution of her case. At the same time, the amount so fixed cannot be excessive or extortionate." CA No. 258/2024 Vardhman Jain & Anr. Vs. Richi Singhal Page no. 11 of 21 19. Further, Hon'ble Apex Court in case titled as Rajnesh Vs Neha & Anr, Crl. Appeal No. 730/2020 (arising out of SLP (Crl) No. 9503/2018, dated 04.11.2020 has held as under :- Criteria for determining quantum of maintenance :- The objective of granting interim / permanent alimony is to ensure that the dependent spouse is not reduced to destitution or vagrancy on account of the failure of the marriage, and not as a punishment to the other spouse. There is no straitjacket formula for fixing the quantum of maintenance to be awarded. The factors which would weigh with the Court inter alia are the status of the parties; reasonable needs of the wife and dependent children; whether the applicant is educated and professionally qualified; whether the applicant has any independent source of income; whether the income is sufficient to enable her to maintain the same standard of living as she was accustomed to in her matrimonial home; whether the applicant was employed prior to her marriage; whether she was working during the subsistence of the marriage; whether the wife was required to sacrifice her employment opportunities for nurturing the family, child rearing, and looking after adult members of the family; reasonable costs of litigation for a nonworking wife. Vardhman Jain vs Richi Singhal on 17 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151189958/ 6 20. The court must take into consideration the status of the parties and the capacity of the spouse to pay for her or her child or his support, the financial capacity of the husband, his actual income, reasonable expenses for his own maintenance and dependent family members including his own child, whom he is obliged to maintain under the law, liabilities if any, would be required to be taken into consideration. The CA No. 258/2024 Vardhman Jain & Anr. Vs. Richi Singhal Page no. 12 of 21 Court must have due regard to the standard of living of the husband, as well as the spiraling inflation rates and high costs of living. The plea of the husband that he does not possess any such source of income through which, he could maintain her wife and child, ipso facto does not absolve him of his moral duty to maintain his wife or his child if he is able bodied and has educational qualifications. One of the ground on which respondents seeks setting aside of impugned order is that complainant is a well qualified woman and is capable of earning. Hon'ble Apex Court in case titled as Rajnesh Vs Neha & Anr (Supra) has held as under :- (c) Where wife is earning some income. The Courts have held that if the wife is earning, it cannot operate as a bar from being awarded maintenance by the husband. The Courts have provided guidance on this issue in the following judgments. 22. In the present matter, it claimed by the respondent/ appellant that the complainant of earning, the appellant has failed to substantiate the aforesaid averments by placing on record any cogent evidence to show that the complainant was ever employed in the past. It is also to be seen CA No. 258/2024 Vardhman Jain & Anr. Vs. Richi Singhal Page no. 13 of 21 that the minor child between the parties has been residing with the complainant and it cannot be lost sight that the complainant being mother on her own alone, has been looking after the minor child since the separation and it is difficult to leave the child alone and take up any employment. The aforesaid ground is devoid of merit and therefore, is discarded and dismissed. 23. Further, there is another issue that complainant and their child are residing at the same address where the respondents are residing and the respondents are taking care of all the expenses of the minor child like school fees, tuition fees, uniforms, books, stationary and other curricular activities, clothes and medicines etc. It is also argued that since the complainant in the matrimonial home on a separate floor, there is no requirement for granting maintenance for boarding and lodging and therefore the impugned order is liable to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. 24. Ld. Counsel for the complainant Richi Singhal has argued that the in present matter, the complainant was abandoned by the respondents and due to the domestic violence committed upon her, she filed the present complaint against the respondent. Later on, the complainant shifted to a separate floor in the same premises as that of the respondent with the minor child and since then has been taking care of the minor child. It has been argued that aforesaid fact has already been dealt and appreciated by Ld. Trial Court vide impugned order in 'para 28' and therefore, there is no Vardhman Jain vs Richi Singhal on 17 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151189958/ 7 infirmity in order of Ld. Trial Court and impugned order is correct and does not require interference. CA No. 258/2024 Vardhman Jain & Anr. Vs. Richi Singhal Page no. 14 of 21 25. 28. The Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the case of Lavlesh Shukla v Rukmani, Crl. Rev. No. 851/2019 , has held that where the wife is unemployed and is incurring expenses towards maintaining herself and the minor child / children, she is entitled to receive maintenance from the date of application. Maintenance is awarded to a wife to overcome the financial crunch, which occurs on account of her separation from her husband. It is neither a matter of favour to the wife, nor any charity done by the husband. Besides, paying tuition fee, stationary etc. there are other requirements for daily needs of complainant and her child. CA No. 258/2024 Vardhman Jain & Anr. Vs. Richi Singhal Page no. 17 of 21 29. Further, in order to determine the quantum of maintenance payable to an applicant, the Court shall take into account the criteria enumerated in Part B - III of the judgment Rajnesh Vs Neha and Anr. (supra). The objective of granting interim / permanent alimony is to ensure that the dependent spouse is not reduced to destitution or vagrancy on account of the failure of the marriage, and not as a punishment to the other spouse. An able-bodied husband must be presumed to be capable of earning sufficient money to maintain his wife and children and cannot contend that he is not in a position to earn sufficiently to maintain his family or the child, as held by the Delhi High Court in Chander Prakash Bodhraj v Shila Rani Chander Prakash. 31. The onus is on the husband to establish with necessary material that there are sufficient grounds to show that he is unable to maintain the family and discharge his legal obligations for reasons beyond his control. Further, the obligation of the husband to provide maintenance to her wife or child, stands on a higher pedestal than the wife. CA No. 258/2024 Vardhman Jain & Anr. Vs. Richi Singhal Page no. 18 of 21 Vardhman Jain vs Richi Singhal on 17 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151189958/ 9 32. Under section 20 DV Act, the magistrate has powers to direct husband to pay monetary relief to meet the expenses incurred and losses suffered by the aggrieved person and any child of the aggrieved person as a result of the domestic violence and such relief may inter alia include the maintenance for aggrieved person as well as her children. 33. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case law titled as Dr. Kulbhushan Kunwar v. Raj Kumari (1970) 3 SCC 129, has held, which as under :- "12. Section 125 Cr.P.C. stipulates that if any person having sufficient means neglects or refuses to maintain his wife, his legitimate or illegitimate minor child, who are otherwise unable to maintain themselves, shall be obligated to do so. A moral duty and a statutory obligation is cast upon the husband to maintain his wife, minor children, parents who otherwise are not capable of maintaining themselves. Merely giving the details CA No. 258/2024 Vardhman Jain & Anr. Vs. Richi Singhal Page no. 19 of 21 of expenses by the respondent/ husband does not absolve him of his liability to maintain his wife and child. 35. Therefore, in view of the aforesaid discussions, though the net monthly income of respondent/ husband is assessed to be Rs.1,00,000/-, however, it is held that there is no infirmity in the impugned order whereby respondent/ husband has been directed to pay maintenance of Rs. 50000/- for the complainant and their minor child. Further, considering the fact that respondent has legal obligation being father of minor child and husband of complainant, I am of the considered opinion that respondent/ appellant Vardhman Jain, is capable of paying the maintenance as awarded by Ld. Trial Court to the complainant and their minor child. CA No. 258/2024 Vardhman Jain & Anr. Vs. Richi Singhal Page no. 20 of 21 Vardhman Jain vs Richi Singhal on 17 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151189958/ 10 37.
